newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE Mar white sugar breaks support, bounces back.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE Mar white sugar breaks support, bounces back.

text.p: London's March white sugar contract briefly broke critical chart support at $300 per tonne on Friday but then bounced back to hover above its opening level, traders said.

But even with the expected test of support, activity was described as dull with a good part of the modest volume deriving from crossed trades.Trade and commission house players were reported to have been the most active during the session. The March white premium attracted light buying around $68 but is expected to narrow further, market sources said.
At 1645 GMT the front spread had once again moved into a slight contango. March was $1.20 higher at $303.00 and May was up 70 cents at $303.30. Overall volume reached 1,685 lots.

Traders said prices were still fundamentally weak with heavy supply overhanging the market and relatively few buyers. "You've got the sellers chasing the buyers. It'll gradually wear itself down -- the hope is that as the market comes off, you'll gradually pick up buyers along the way," said one.
"The whites market will probably remain under pressure for most of the year," he said.
Positions also weakened on the Paris market but ranges were not as wide as in London.
The spot March contract managed to hold above $300.00, scoring an intraday low of $301.50, standing 30 cents lower at $302.50. May was 60 cents lower at $302.70 and Matif volume was a light 155 lots.
